title: True-up reconciler for reserved capacity discounts and retroactive rate adjustments
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build a reconciliation service (true-up reconciler) that applies reserved-capacity discounts, handles retroactive rate adjustments, and corrects late-arriving usage events for tenant billing. The reconciler must produce auditable corrections (positive or negative) per-tenant, keep a clear provenance chain, and output finalized charge events for downstream invoicing. It should be tolerant of out-of-order events and provide deterministic, idempotent application of adjustments.
background_and_rationale: Customers on Dedicated/reserved plans occasionally receive usage credits or are subject to post-hoc pricing changes (promotions, negotiated discounts, or contract overrides). Our current streaming metering pipeline inconsistently applies reserved-plan discounts when late events arrive or when rate tables change retroactively, causing invoice corrections and support load. This ticket implements a reconciler that ensures predictable true-ups and provides tools for operators to inspect, revert, or manually approve large adjustments.
technical_design: Core components: 1) Delta ingestion layer that consumes canonical usage events and rate-change events (from rate-service and contract table) into an append-only reconciliation topic. 2) Time-windowed state machine per-tenant that computes effective rate per token considering reservation commitments, tier caps, and negotiated overrides. 3) Deterministic correction generator that emits idempotent correction records to the billing ledger with provenance metadata (source_event_ids, applied_rules, calculation_hash). 4) Export job to produce audit CSVs for invoicing and support. Implementation will use a Stateful Flink job (or our existing stream processor) with RocksDB state and checkpointing, backed by a reconciliation table in Spanner for fast lookups and backfills.
acceptance_criteria: Reconciler consumes historical and streaming usage events and produces correction records where effective rate differs from initial charge
Corrections are idempotent: reprocessing the same input range does not create duplicates
Provenance metadata is stored with every correction (origin event IDs, applied discount ids, timestamp)
Automated tests cover: late-arriving event up to 72 hours, retroactive rate table change, negotiated override precedence rules
End-to-end pipeline latency for reconciliation run under normal load < 6 hours for 30-day backfill; streaming corrections emitted within target SLA of 15 minutes after input arrival
Regression dashboards: number and dollar-amount of corrections per tenant, per-release smoke tests pass
Operators can run a manual true-up for a tenant via an internal Console action; the job logs an audit trail and produces an approval ticket if adjustment exceeds threshold
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch + unit/integration tests. 2) Deploy reconciler in dry-run mode that emits corrections to a shadow topic (no ledger writes) for 1 week against last 30 days of data. 3) Run manual validation with Finance & Support on sampled tenants. 4) Enable corrections to staging ledger for two test tenants. 5) Gradual rollout to production with canary set (5% of tenants), monitor correction rates and customer complaints, then full enablement.
migration_steps: - Backfill last 90 days in a batch job to compute baseline corrections. - Mark current ledger entries with reconciliation_version. - Apply corrections in small batches during low-traffic windows. - Provide a rollback path: cancel corrections via inverse correction records and mark reconciliation_version as deprecated.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: reconciliation throughput, corrections per minute, dollar-volume of corrections, percent of tenants with corrections. Alerts: spike in corrections (>3x baseline in 1h), correction job failures, checkpoint lag > 10 minutes. Create a runbook for on-call to triage large or unexpected true-ups.
testing_plan: Unit tests for calculation logic and precedence rules. Integration tests against a synthetic usage/event generator to simulate out-of-order arrival and rate-table changes. Staging dry-run end-to-end tests validating shadow corrections against expected golden outputs. Prepare dataset and asserts for finance to validate totals.
tradeoffs_and_alternatives: Option A (chosen): Stateful streaming reconciler with deterministic idempotent outputs; pros: near-real-time corrections, smaller operational overhead for incremental updates; cons: complexity in state management. Option B: Periodic batch true-up (daily) using Spark; pros: simpler semantics and easier backfills; cons: slower, higher latency for corrections, worse UX for customers expecting quick crediting. We chose A due to latency expectations from enterprise customers.
security_and_compliance: All correction outputs and provenance metadata must be written to encrypted storage and audited. Ensure role-based access for manual true-up triggers and that any customer PII in events is redacted before export. Finance sign-off required before enabling prod writes.
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Initial design doc created and shared with Billing + Platform teams. (https://confluence.redwood.ai/billing/true-up-design)
2025-02-20: Spike completed evaluating Flink vs internal streamrunner; selected internal streamrunner for compatibility with existing checkpointing. Performance microbenchmarks attached.

2025-02-26: Proof-of-concept computes corrections for sample tenant set; identified corner case where negotiated overrides overlap promotional discounts (resolved precedence rule: negotiated > reserved > promo)
2025-03-01: Dry-run pipeline deployed to staging in shadow mode; produced shadow corrections for last 30 days. Finance review scheduled 2025-03-05.
2025-03-04: Implemented idempotency via calculation_hash + reconciliation_run_id. Integration tests added for late-arriving events up to 72 hours.
open_questions: What is the threshold for automatic vs manual approval of large negative corrections? (Finance input needed)
Should negotiated overrides be stored in a dedicated materialized view or read live from the contracts service?
Do we accept corrections that change historical invoice periods, or should we only emit credit notes in subsequent billing cycles?
next_steps: Address finance approval thresholds and update acceptance criteria
Complete integration tests for promotional overlap scenarios
Add operator Console UI for manual true-up trigger and approval flow
Schedule production dry-run with real tenant subset after Finance sign-off
